Connected Sets

This scene is about connected sets. Move the cut point and check whether the set splits into two open pieces that never touch.

A set that cannot be split is connected. An interval never splits: wherever you cut, the cut point itself belongs to neither side. Two far-apart pieces, or the rationals with their dense gaps, split cleanly when the cut lands in a gap.

For example, look at one 🧩 jigsaw puzzle. While the pieces interlock, it is a single board. Lying in two completely separate piles, it is already split apart.

Prove completely that if XXX is path-connected then XXX is connected.

Path-connected means that for any a,b∈Xa, b \in Xa,b∈X there is a continuous γ:[0,1]→X\gamma : [0,1] \to Xγ:[0,1]→X with γ(0)=a\gamma(0) = aγ(0)=a and γ(1)=b\gamma(1) = bγ(1)=b.

You may use Problem 1 (connectedness of [0,1][0,1][0,1]).

    The converse is false: the closure of the topologist's sine curve is connected but not path-connected.
